Review: cc-audit 3.17.25 and two native SORA/Mirai builds

BENIGN e5112ac4366709ba0fe0f1924a4f6897dfab203b7ff3e8f394effb62ebd16d5e
Rust security auditor source archive, not an installed malicious skill.
README/Cargo metadata identify ryo-ebata/cc-audit. handlers/scan.rs drives
user-requested scans and report writes; rules/builtin/exfiltration.rs compiles
regular expressions, rather than performing the transfers described by them.
The examples/bypass-attempts scripts demonstrate hostile operations as a
scanner test corpus. The npm wrapper selects platform-specific binaries via
optional dependencies, with no install lifecycle script. The current scan
has no hostile or suspicious traits; no new blanket exclusions were added.
No hostile fetched-dependency finding was observed.

MALICIOUS 729238bab5e3bb8ada801a6389cf2ebcbf1d6313d772ac20f998771248f9556f
UPX-packed static ARM EABI5 Linux SORA/Mirai bot. A copy was unpacked; the
original was not executed or modified. rizin identifies ARM and .text/.rodata.
Unpacked VAs: 0x1a3a8 iterates the table and XORs each byte with the four
bytes of the stored key; 0x1a440 allocates and copies encoded table entries.
0x1a4a8 references the CNC banner at 0x778a8; the same table contains the
Source Engine Query string, Telnet dialogue, SORA busybox probe, kill -9,
and procfs/watchdog paths. The full default credential table and networking
syscall constants support credential scanning, with a registered attack table.

MALICIOUS 9ea1f8e83c99a88df3c938529d76d343cca7fbb37c3948f1560a2b39da2bd4ab
Static stripped little-endian Linux SuperH SORA/Mirai bot. ELF e_machine=42.
rizin VAs: main 0x40042c; attack registration 0x400b4c; encoded table init
0x4089e8; bytewise four-key XOR loop 0x408978; table retrieval 0x408d44.
The table includes shell/enable/login/password/failure dialogue, SORA probes,
process enumeration/termination commands, CNC banner and VSE query. Decoded
default passwords include vizxv, xc3551, hi3518 and 7ujMko0 variants. The
embedded host is 103.170.217.170. Direct socket wrapper 0x414c34 loads 340;
connect wrapper 0x4144e4 loads 342. Both use trapa 0x13. Numbers checked
against Linux arch/sh/kernel/syscalls/syscall.tbl (upstream primary source).

Trait corrections:
- Add neutral SuperH socket/connect wrapper evidence, with PC-load-to-literal
  binding and .text scope; do not classify libc networking as suspicious.
- Remove the neutral client helper from the brute-force objective namespace;
  keep the dialer alternatives in that objective's required networking role.
- Count distinct complete credential variants, not overlapping prefixes.
- Require Telnet shell/scan dialogue for the Telnet attack composite.
- Replace the architecture/path-based VSE verdicts with credential scanner,
  SORA credential/VSE family signature and attack-context DDoS detection.
  Watchdog paths do not prove systemd persistence, reactivation or feeding.
- Tighten DDoS admission with credential-table and encoded CNC evidence.
- Describe procfs paths as references, not demonstrated reads.

Controls:
network-client.elf is a minimal synthetic SH ELF containing only the two
libc wrapper bodies. It must match neutral networking and no hostile trait.
wrong-syscalls.elf changes the literals to bind/listen (341/343).
wrong-literal-targets.elf changes the PC-relative displacements. Both must
fail the socket/connect matchers despite preserving traps and nearby numbers.
The wrappers are ordinary libc code, without specimen-specific addresses,
hashes, filenames or C2 values in the new matchers.

Verification: atomscan --no-update --mode slow with CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR pointing
at this checkout and CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1 found zero hostile/suspicious traits
in the cc-audit archive and its fetched artifacts (846 report files), and
three hostile traits in each native bot. Reports are in the named workspace
scratch/triage directory. All three neutral networking controls passed.
The hostile scanner, DDoS and family composites matched the SuperH sample
with precision scores above 3.5 (12.4, 15.4 and 14.0 respectively).
Primary syscall-number reference:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/arch/sh/kernel/syscalls/syscall.tbl
